items.source_name: VA Multiple Sclerosis Centers of Excellence — Creating a Support Network + MS-Related Fatigue
items.source_locator: VA Multiple Sclerosis Centers of Excellence — Creating a Support Network: sections ‘What is a support network?’ and ‘What is a support group?’; supplemental official VA MS-Related Fatigue page, ‘Managing Fatigue’ practical planning strategies.
items.source_version: VA support-network page last updated 2024-02-13; VA MS-Related Fatigue page current in 2026; both rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Joining a peer support group, seeking reliable disease information, and making a practical fatigue-management plan are adaptive coping and self-management behaviors. VA MS guidance supports building an individualized support network and using practical strategies to manage fatigue; these behaviors increase support and day-to-day control rather than demonstrating denial or regression.

items.source_locator: DailyMed morphine sulfate label — Geriatric Use and Warnings/Precautions on life-threatening respiratory depression: cautious low-end geriatric dosing and monitoring during initiation/titration.
items.source_version: Current FDA labeling at the exact DailyMed URL/set identity; live version rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Older adults can have increased opioid sensitivity and reduced renal, hepatic, or cardiac reserve. Morphine should be individualized, generally starting cautiously at the low end in geriatric patients, then titrated to analgesic effect while monitoring sedation, respiratory depression, renal function, concomitant sedatives, and other risk factors.

items.source_locator: DailyMed PITOCIN label — Administration, Induction or Stimulation of Labor, Monitoring: continuously monitor uterine activity/FHR and discontinue immediately for uterine hyperactivity and/or fetal distress.
items.source_version: Current PITOCIN FDA label displayed by DailyMed in 2026; exact label URL rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Six contractions in 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes meets the definition of uterine tachysystole. When tachysystole occurs during oxytocin administration—especially with recurrent fetal heart-rate decelerations—the oxytocin should be reduced or stopped according to protocol and intrauterine resuscitative measures and prompt reassessment initiated.

items.source_locator: DailyMed RhoGAM Ultra-Filtered PLUS label — Indications/Usage and obstetric dosing: prevention of Rh immunization, routine antepartum prophylaxis at 26–28 weeks and postpartum prophylaxis when indicated.
items.source_version: Current FDA RhoGAM label at the exact DailyMed set ID; live version rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Rho(D) immune globulin provides passive anti-D that suppresses maternal immunization after exposure to Rh-positive fetal red cells. It prevents sensitization; it does not treat established fetal hemolytic disease or change fetal Rh type. Antepartum prophylaxis does not automatically eliminate postpartum dosing when the newborn is Rh-positive.

items.source_name: CDC — Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women
items.source_locator: CDC Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women — MMR: live attenuated MMR is contraindicated during pregnancy; vaccinate after pregnancy when indicated.
items.source_version: Current CDC pregnancy-vaccination guidance at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: MMR is a live attenuated viral vaccine and is contraindicated during pregnancy because of theoretical fetal risk. A rubella-nonimmune pregnant patient should receive MMR after pregnancy when indicated. Tdap and inactivated influenza vaccination are recommended during pregnancy according to current schedules.

items.source_version: Current FDA theophylline label at exact DailyMed set ID; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range. Nausea/vomiting, tremor, palpitations and tachyarrhythmias can occur with excessive exposure. Erythromycin can inhibit theophylline clearance and raise concentrations. When toxicity is suspected, labeling advises withholding additional theophylline and measuring the serum concentration promptly.

items.source_locator: DailyMed clindamycin hydrochloride capsules — BOXED WARNING for C. difficile-associated diarrhea/colitis, including severe or fatal disease during or after antibacterial therapy.
items.source_version: DailyMed label version 35 at the exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: New frequent watery diarrhea and cramping during clindamycin therapy require evaluation for C. difficile-associated diarrhea. The boxed warning notes that CDAD can be severe or fatal and can occur even after antibiotic exposure. Unsupervised antimotility treatment or simply continuing therapy without assessment can be unsafe.

items.source_locator: DailyMed terbutaline sulfate injection — BOXED WARNING on prolonged tocolysis and maternal cardiovascular/metabolic adverse effects including tachycardia, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema and myocardial ischemia.
items.source_version: Current FDA terbutaline injection label at exact DailyMed set ID; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Terbutaline is a beta-agonist and can cause maternal tachycardia, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, myocardial ischemia, hypokalemia, and hyperglycemia. It is not FDA-approved for prolonged tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours and must not be used for outpatient maintenance tocolysis. New cardiovascular or respiratory symptoms require urgent review.

items.source_version: DailyMed CIPRO version 32/current 2026 label at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Fluoroquinolones, including ciprofloxacin, can cause tendinitis and tendon rupture, sometimes with disabling or irreversible adverse effects. New tendon pain or swelling during therapy warrants stopping the fluoroquinolone and prompt clinical review, with avoidance of exercise or loading of the affected tendon until evaluated.

items.source_locator: The Joint Commission FAQ 000001226, Medical Equipment — Defibrillator and Crash Cart: crash carts/defibrillators are high-risk equipment and battery charge requires a defined maintenance process; FAQ 000001073 requires a defined process to monitor emergency-cart integrity/contents.

items.source_version: Current OSHA eTool at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: OSHA recommends confirming a safe evacuation path before approaching a fire, selecting the appropriate extinguisher, and using PASS: pull the pin, aim low at the base, squeeze the handle, and sweep side to side. If the extinguisher is empty, the fire grows, or the user is unsure of safe control, evacuation is the priority.

items.source_locator: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices — PPE removal/hand hygiene: remove and discard PPE to avoid contaminating skin/clothing and perform hand hygiene; sequence depends on ensemble/workflow.
items.source_version: Current CDC Core Practices at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: The safety goal during doffing is to prevent self-contamination. CDC provides example sequences, but the exact order can vary with the PPE ensemble and isolation workflow. Staff should use the approved sequence, avoid touching contaminated PPE surfaces to skin or clothing, dispose of PPE appropriately, and perform hand hygiene.

items.source_version: Current OSHA federal requirements at exact URL; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: OSHA requires work-related needlestick injuries from sharps contaminated with another person's blood or other potentially infectious material to be recorded when the employer is subject to Part 1904 recordkeeping. Option D confuses social determinants with utilization management and payer authorization.
